No, just x86-64 asm. Or whatever is the fastest currently on x86-64. There is an optimization when you use at most 255 bits out of the 256 bits, it would work for BN254, it's 15% faster by saving some carries, or do you want the generic one? with the optim, this is the fastest: https://github.com/mratsim/constantine/blob/master/constantine/math/arithmetic/assembly/limbs_asm_mul_mont_x86_adx_bmi2.nim#L231-L240 I don't have asm without the optim because all pairing curves (BN254, BLS12-381) have spare bits, unlike secp256k1 for example For generic one, here you go: https://github.com/mratsim/constantine/blob/master/constantine/math/arithmetic/limbs_montgomery.nim#L215-L305 FIPS is faster than CIOS (unless you use MULX/ADOX/ADCX) <@774033563732541451> <@750602516613431366> I'm reading this https://ihagopian.com/posts/tonelli-shanks-with-precomputed-dlog-tables Have you tried https://eprint.iacr.org/2020/1407.pdf `Computing Square Roots Faster than the Tonelli-Shanks/Bernstein Algorithm` I'll defer having a good answer to that to <@750602516613431366> or <@761645159095599144> . I want to make a performance baseline (how fast we can go with the best montgomery multiplication and very simple EVMMAX-like API) spare, yes Is this nim code direct implementation or it generates asm code? <@570268431522201601> , very interesting work https://github.com/mratsim/constantine Do you have an idea how much performance (and where) is left on the table due to the design decision of having constant-time algorithms? excerpts.author: mratsim
excerpts.content: with 256-bit integers in the EVM? Mmmh not really

excerpts.author: mratsim
excerpts.content:
Faster than any other library out there: BLST, Barrentenberg, Arkworks, Bellman, ...

Only Gnark can reach similar speed (but 10% slower on the number of cores I benched).

- SIngle-threaded benches: https://github.com/mratsim/constantine/pull/220
- Multi-threaded on 8 cores: https://github.com/mratsim/constantine/pull/226#issuecomment-1505143179
- Multi-threaded in 18 cores: https://github.com/mratsim/constantine/pull/227#issuecomment-1508372663

Note that the Gnark team has been tuning on 96 cores and I don't have such a machine so I may be slower on very large core counts.
